'''Harry Barkus Gray''' (born November 14, 1935) is the Arnold O. Beckman Professor of Chemistry at [[California Institute of Technology]].<ref name="Caltech">{{cite web|title=Harry B. Gray|url=http://www.cce.caltech.edu/content/harry-b-gray|website=California Institute of Technology|access-date=October 25, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170810170306/http://www.cce.caltech.edu/content/harry-b-gray|archive-date=August 10, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Career==
Gray received his B.S. in chemistry from [[Western Kentucky University]] in 1957. He began his work in [[inorganic chemistry]] at [[Northwestern University]], where he earned his Ph.D. in 1960 working under [[Fred Basolo]] and [[Ralph Pearson]]. He was initiated into the Upsilon chapter of [[Alpha Chi Sigma]] at Northwestern University in 1958.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.alphachisigma.org/Page.aspx?pid=463|title=Educational Foundation - Alpha Chi Sigma|publisher=Alphachisigma.org|access-date=February 14, 2015}}</ref> After that, he spent a year (1960–61) as an [[National Science Foundation|NSF]] Postdoctoral Fellow at the [[University of Copenhagen]],<ref name="WKU">{{cite web|title=Dr. Harry B. Gray (Inducted in 1995)|url=http://alumni.wku.edu/s/808/media.aspx?pgid=1733&gid=1|website=Western Kentucky University|access-date=October 25, 2016}}</ref> where, along with Walter A. Manch, he collaborated with Carl J. Ballhausen on studies of the electronic structures of metal complexes.<ref name="Avery">{{cite book|last1=Avery|first1=John|last2=Dahl|first2=Jens Peder|last3=Hansen|first3=Aage E.|title=Understanding Molecular Properties a Symposium in Honour of Professor Carl Johan Ballhausen, held at The Royal Danish Academy of Sciences and Letters, April 4 and 5, 1986|date=1987|publisher=Springer Netherlands|location=Dordrecht|isbn=978-94-009-3781-9|pages=ix–x|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=l0LvCAAAQBAJ&pg=PR9|access-date=October 25, 2016}}</ref><ref name="Phillips">{{cite web|title=Francis Clifford Phillips Lecture Series 1986 Phillips Lecturer Brief Biography of Harry Gray, California Institute of Technology|url=http://www.pitt.edu/~plu/pl/gray.htm|website=Phi Lambda Upsilon Xi Chapter, University of Pittsburgh|access-date=October 25, 2016|archive-date=November 17, 2002|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20021117230318/http://www.pitt.edu/~plu/pl/gray.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref>

After completing his NSF Postdoctoral Fellowship at the [[University of Copenhagen]], he relocated to New York City to take up a faculty appointment at [[Columbia University]]. He served as an assistant professor from 1961 to 1963 and as an associate professor from 1963 to 1965.

In 1966, he became the Arnold O. Beckman Professor of Chemistry at [[California Institute of Technology]], and founding director of the [[Beckman Institute at Caltech|Beckman Institute]].<ref name="BILRC">{{cite web|url=http://www.bilrc.caltech.edu/index.php?module=webpage&var1=16|title=Harry B. Gray|website=Beckman Institute Laser Resource Center|access-date=October 25, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170810212026/https://www.bilrc.caltech.edu//index.php?module=webpage&var1=16|archive-date=August 10, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> He also served on the Physical Sciences jury for the [[Infosys Prize]] from 2010 to 2013.

Gray also trained future leaders of several major science research universities. Four of his doctoral students became presidents or chancellors: [[David M. Dooley]] at [[University of Rhode Island]], [[Gregory L. Geoffroy]] at [[Iowa State University]], [[Holden Thorp]] at [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]], and [[Mark S. Wrighton|Mark Wrighton]] at [[Washington University in St. Louis]].<ref>{{cite magazine |date=May 6, 2015 |title=Leading By Example |url=https://magazine.caltech.edu/esblog/leading-by-example |magazine=E&S Magazine |publisher=California Institute of Technology}}</ref>

==Research==
Gray's interdisciplinary research program addresses a wide range of fundamental problems in [[inorganic chemistry]], [[biochemistry]], and [[biophysics]]. [[Electron transfer]] (ET) chemistry is a unifying theme for much of this research.<ref name="Jacoby"/>

Over the past twenty-five years the Gray group has been measuring the kinetics of long-range ET reactions in metalloproteins labeled with inorganic [[redox]] reagents. Early research by his lab members showed that details of the internal structures of the proteins dominate the ET rates.<ref name=Science>{{cite journal|last1=Beratan|last2=Betts|first2=JN|last3=Onuchic|first3=JN|date=1991|first1=DN|title=Protein electron transfer rates set by the bridging secondary and tertiary structure|journal=Science|volume=252|issue=5010|pages=1285–8|url=https://www.science.org/doi/abs/10.1126/science.1656523|publisher=Sciencemag.orgaccessdate=June 18, 2013|doi=10.1126/science.1656523|pmid=1656523|bibcode=1991Sci...252.1285B|display-authors=etal|url-access=subscription}}</ref>  Current research is aimed at understanding how intermediate protein radicals accelerate long-range ET. In collaboration with [[Jay R. Winkler]] of the [[Beckman Institute at Caltech]] they have developed new techniques for measuring ET rates in crystals of Ru-, Os-, and Re-modified [[azurin]]s, as well as crystals of Fe(III)-[[cytochrome c]] doped with Zn(II)-cytochrome c.<ref name="Winkler">{{cite journal|last1=Winkler|first1=Jay R.|last2=Gray|first2=Harry B.|title=Electron flow through biological molecules: does hole hopping protect proteins from oxidative damage?|journal=Quarterly Reviews of Biophysics|date=July 16, 2015|volume=48|issue=4|pages=411–420|doi=10.1017/S0033583515000062|pmc=4793975|pmid=26537399}}</ref> This method of integrating [[photosensitizers]] into protein crystals has provided a powerful new tool for studying biochemical reaction dynamics.<ref name="Tezcan">{{cite journal|last1=Tezcan|first1=F. Akif|last2=Crane|first2=Brian R.|last3=Winkler|first3=Jay R.|last4=Gray|first4=Harry B.|title=Electron Tunneling in Protein Crystals|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America|date=2001|volume=98|issue=9|pages=5002–5006|jstor=3055554|doi=10.1073/pnas.081072898|pmid=11296248|bibcode=2001PNAS...98.5002A|pmc=33153|doi-access=free}}</ref> The Gray/Winkler group is also using ET chemistry to probe the dynamics of [[protein folding]] in [[cytochrome c]].<ref name="Mines">{{cite journal|last1=Mines|first1=Gary A.|last2=Pascher|first2=Torbjörn|last3=Lee|first3=Sonny C.|last4=Winkler|first4=Jay R.|last5=Gray|first5=Harry B.|title=Cytochrome c folding triggered by electron transfer|journal=Chemistry & Biology|date=June 1996|volume=3|issue=6|pages=491–497|doi=10.1016/S1074-5521(96)90097-6|pmid=8807879|doi-access=free}}</ref>

===Wolf Prize===
He was awarded the [[Wolf Prize in Chemistry]] in 2004 for his pioneering work in [[bioinorganic chemistry]], unraveling novel principles of structure and long-range [[electron transfer]] in proteins.<ref name="Jacoby">{{cite journal|last1=Jacoby|first1=Mitch|title=AWARDS Harry Gray Wins Wolf Prize In Chemistry|journal=Chemical & Engineering News|date=January 26, 2004|volume=82|issue=4|url=http://pubs.acs.org/cen/topstory/8204/8204notw5.html|access-date=October 25, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://bilrc.caltech.edu/BILRC-HBG/HBG_CV.pdf|title=Beckman Institute Laser Resource Center|publisher=Bilrc.caltech.org|access-date=February 14, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080907123252/http://bilrc.caltech.edu/BILRC-HBG/HBG_CV.pdf|archive-date=September 7, 2008|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Gray has made generative contributions to the understanding of chemical bonding of metal complexes, mechanisms of inorganic reactions, spectroscopy and magneto-chemistry of inorganic compounds. His study of the first trigonal prismatic complexes is one such example. Harry Gray's most significant work lies at the interface between [[chemistry]] and [[biology]]. As a pioneer of the important and thriving field of [[bioinorganic chemistry]], he has made many key contributions, the most important of which is the development of fundamental understanding of electron transfer in biological systems, at the atomic level.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.wolffund.org.il/full.asp?id=147|title=תוצאות חיפוש - פרס וולף|author=Simply-Smart|publisher=Wolffund.org.il|access-date=February 14, 2015}}</ref>
